title: S090 16.1.4 Rules for When to Use Message Body Tags and Last-Modified Dates
parent_path: S090 16.1.4 Rules for When to Use Message Body Tags and Last-Modified Dates

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SHOULD send a message body tag validator unless it is not feasible to generate one.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: MAY send a weak message body tag instead of a strong message body tag, if performance considerations support the use of weak message body tags, or if it is unfeasible to send a strong message body tag.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SHOULD send a Last-Modified value if it is feasible to send one, unless the risk of a breakdown in semantic transparency that could result from using this date in an If-Modified-Since header would lead to serious problems.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In order to be legal, a strong message body tag MUST change whenever the associated entity value changes in any way.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A weak message body tag SHOULD change whenever the associated entity changes in a semantically significant way.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: in order to provide semantically transparent caching, an origin server MUST avoid reusing a specific strong message body tag value for two different entities or reusing a specific weak message body tag value for two semantically different entities.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a message body tag has been provided by the origin server, MUST use that message body tag in any cache-conditional request (using If-Match or If-None-Match).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If only a Last-Modified value has been provided by the origin server, SHOULD use that value in non-subrange cache-conditional requests (using If-Modified-Since).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If both a message body tag and a Last-Modified value have been provided by the origin server, SHOULD use both validators in cache-conditional requests.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An RTSP origin server, upon receiving a conditional request that includes both a Last-Modified date (e.g., in an If-Modified-Since header) and one or more message body tags (e.g., in an If-Match, If-None-Match, or If-Range header field) as cache validators, MUST NOT return a response status of 304 (Not Modified) unless doing so is consistent with all of the conditional header fields in the request.
